comparabilityJudgment.ucr-1: Combined target materially includes development sociology, social theory, cultural meanings, inequality and empirical inquiry. Four sociology/methods courses plus sustained Indigenous/cultural/gender history, heritage, media and global social/political study provide a substantive response. This is not inferred merely from coherence. Specialist anthropology, kinship, ethnographic fieldwork and thesis gaps remain explicit.
comparabilityJudgment.ucr-2: Retains sociology, qualitative research, Indigenous/colonial perspectives and social power while adding sustained environmental justice/governance, ecology and food-system study. Rights replaces technicalEarthtools; sustainablefarming replaces biogeochemistry. Scientific courses have a defined complementary ecological role; they are not described as anthropology or as automatically teaching unequal exposure.

preservationChallenge: The two legal courses in the broad programme were independently defensible and retained after reviewing actual legal/social/normative and comparative-law content. A different reasonable palette alone does not warrant replacement. Private-law rationale narrowed to property/contract/tort institutions rather than anthropology of kinship.
thirdCandidate: Migration/belonging is evidenced, but available advanced UCR content cannot sustain a distinct24courseprogramme without substituting legal/political context for defining mobility/ethnographic substance. The unavailablePublicPolicyAnalysis course was not selected.
modalSourceReview: Every selected current modal description was compared with actual enriched profile/description2. For SustainableFarming the detailed cached list matches description2; profile provides broader outline-derived confirmation. No universal display-field preference was imposed.
